Fill missing continuous cells by their conditional expectation

Source: R/imputeCellGLoc.R
dot-gloc_impute.Rd

A missing cell is imputed by its conditional expectation given the usable peers in its row: the observed cells that pass the detection peer rule (.gloc_peer_rel, i.e. peer_w_min with the peer band). A flagged cell is therefore treated exactly like a missing one, and a peer inside the band is conditioned on with its information discounted, as in .gloc_cond_resid. Until 7.4.0 every observed peer was used, flagged ones included, so a grossly contaminated cell was carried into the imputation of its row-mates; W = NULL still gives that rule.

.gloc_impute(
  X,
  U,
  B,
  Sigma,
  M,
  W = NULL,
  w_min = 0.5,
  band = .gloc_peer_band,
  cov = FALSE
)

Arguments

X

\(n x p\) numeric matrix of continuous variables.

U

\(n x q\) design matrix from .gloc_design.

B

\(q x p\) matrix of mean-structure coefficients.

Sigma

\(p x p\) scatter matrix.

M

\(n x p\) logical mask of missing cells.

W

optional \(n x p\) matrix of cell weights. NULL conditions on every observed peer, the 7.4.0 rule.

w_min, band

the peer rule; see .gloc_peer_rel.

cov

if TRUE, also return the conditional covariance of the missing cells given the same peers, which is what imputation noise must be drawn from.

Value

X with its missing cells replaced. With cov = TRUE, a list with that matrix as X and cond_cov, a list named by row index that holds, for each row with a missing cell, the conditional covariance matrix of its missing cells.

Details

Rows whose peers are all fully in or fully out are grouped by pattern, one matrix inversion per pattern; a row holding a peer inside the band gets a solve of its own. A row with no usable peer falls back to its fitted mean, with the marginal covariance given the design.
